properties.name: text
properties.notes: The string the component draws. `RemoteText` takes a `RemoteString`, so a design's plain string is written as `"…".rs` and a binding or a state value as the remote expression it names — what the design carries is the same JSON either way.

properties.name: style
properties.notes: A role on this catalog's type scale, written as `style = RemoteMaterialTheme.typography.<role>`. This is the way to set type here: a role carries size, weight, line height and letter spacing together through `RemoteTextStyle`, which is why the catalog's own stickers pass a role OR an explicit size and never both. The eighteen are `RemoteTypography`'s own and are NOT the Material 3 fifteen — there is no `headline` on a watch, and there are five `numeral` roles a time or a metric is set in. A role this class does not have would export as a call that does not compile, so the list is exactly what it publishes.

properties.name: fontSize
properties.notes: Size in sp, as an override on top of `style` rather than a substitute for it — set it alone and everything else about the type comes from the ambient style. Spelled the parameter's own way; a design authored against the borrowed `m3/text` says `fontSizeSp` and the writer reads both. A whole number writes `22.rsp`; a fractional one writes `14.5f.sp.asRemoteTextUnit()`, because `RemoteTextUnitKt` publishes no `Float.rsp`.

properties.name: color
properties.notes: A colour: a `#RRGGBB` literal, which exports as `Color(0x…).rc`, or one of `colorTokens.roles`, which exports as `RemoteMaterialTheme.colorScheme.<role>`.

properties.name: fontVariationSettings
properties.notes: Variable-font axis coordinates, CSS `font-variation-settings` style with bare tags: `wght 650, wdth 87.5, GRAD -50`. Written as `RemoteText(fontVariationSettings = FontVariation.Settings(…))`, so the document carries the axes and the player applies them to the face it resolves; an axis that face does not have is ignored. `wght` set here overrides `fontWeight`.

properties.name: fontFeatureSettings
properties.notes: OpenType layout features, CSS `font-feature-settings` style with bare tags: `tnum, ss01, liga 0`. Written as `style = ….merge(fontFeatureSettings = …)`, since `RemoteText` has no feature parameter; Remote Compose carries them in the document beside the axes. A feature the typeface does not have is ignored.

svg.notes: A placeholder on the canvas must not claim structured SVG parity with an animation.

wasm.notes: Drawn as a named placeholder carrying the animation's source and size. The canvas has no Lottie renderer, and compiling the animation the way the export does — into Remote Compose operations — is Horologist's Android-only creation API, which a Wasm build cannot link. A lookalike would be an impression of an animation nobody could check; the picture comes from the native lane, which builds this design's own generated document.

properties.name: showByState
properties.notes: Select one child by state. Object fields: selector is a typed scalar or state read; cases is an object mapping child IDs to typed scalar values; optional fallback is a string child ID. Every child must be a case or the fallback. Compose export uses when. Remote export uses StateLayout for non-null number or flag selectors; String equality is unavailable on that target.

properties.name: verticalArrangement

colorTokens.$comment: The theme roles a colour property may name. Same Material 3 vocabulary as the sibling :catalog, and stated here for the same reason: a Remote design names roles, and a role the canvas cannot resolve is a literal. Every sticker in this catalog is a RemoteDocument carrying explicit dark-first Material colours, so the values behind these names are the document's rather than a theme's — but the names are what a design writes.

propertyCapabilities.name: containerImageKey
propertyCapabilities.notes: The key of an asset to fill the container with, as `asset/image`'s `assetKey`: written as the `containerPainter` overload, `containerPainter = painterRemoteImageBitmap(…)`. A plain container when absent. The record carries the overload without a painter, so this is stated rather than derived.

propertyCapabilities.name: containerImageKey
propertyCapabilities.notes: The key of an asset to fill the container with, as `asset/image`'s `assetKey`: written as the `containerPainter` overload, `containerPainter = painterRemoteImageBitmap(…)`. A plain container when absent. The record carries the overload without a painter, so this is stated rather than derived.

propertyCapabilities.name: pageCount
propertyCapabilities.notes: How many pages there are; 4 when absent. `state` is a `RemotePageIndicatorState`, which no design value becomes, so the emitter builds it from this and `selectedPage`.

propertyCapabilities.name: selectedPage
propertyCapabilities.notes: The page shown, from zero: a literal or the design's Int state, which is how a pager drives the dots. The first when absent.

propertyCapabilities.name: imageVector
propertyCapabilities.notes: A Material icon key (`home`, `search`, `addCircle`, …), written as `Icons.<Style>.<Name>.toRemoteImageVector()` — `RemoteIcon` takes a `RemoteImageVector` captured from the `androidx.compose.material.icons` vector. Unset draws `addCircle`, the default the canvas mapping above gives.

propertyCapabilities.name: contentDescription
propertyCapabilities.notes: What a screen reader says for the icon. Leave it empty beside a label; set it when the icon is the whole button.

propertyCapabilities.name: tint
propertyCapabilities.notes: A colour: a `#RRGGBB` literal or one of `colorTokens.roles`. Unset inherits the enclosing content colour, which is how a button's colour reaches its icon.

remote-m3/remote-sticker.excluded: the catalog's own preview frame, not a Remote Compose component: every sticker is drawn inside one and nobody places one in a design.

propertyCapabilities.name: text
propertyCapabilities.notes: The string the component draws. `RemoteText` takes a `RemoteString`, so a design's plain string is written as `"…".rs` and a binding or a state value as the remote expression it names — what the design carries is the same JSON either way.

propertyCapabilities.name: style
propertyCapabilities.notes: A role on this catalog's type scale, written as `style = RemoteMaterialTheme.typography.<role>`. This is the way to set type here: a role carries size, weight, line height and letter spacing together through `RemoteTextStyle`, which is why the catalog's own stickers pass a role OR an explicit size and never both. The eighteen are `RemoteTypography`'s own and are NOT the Material 3 fifteen — there is no `headline` on a watch, and there are five `numeral` roles a time or a metric is set in. A role this class does not have would export as a call that does not compile, so the list is exactly what it publishes.

propertyCapabilities.name: fontSize
propertyCapabilities.notes: Size in sp, as an override on top of `style` rather than a substitute for it — set it alone and everything else about the type comes from the ambient style. Spelled the parameter's own way; a design authored against the borrowed `m3/text` says `fontSizeSp` and the writer reads both. A whole number writes `22.rsp`; a fractional one writes `14.5f.sp.asRemoteTextUnit()`, because `RemoteTextUnitKt` publishes no `Float.rsp`.

propertyCapabilities.name: color
propertyCapabilities.notes: A colour: a `#RRGGBB` literal, which exports as `Color(0x…).rc`, or one of `colorTokens.roles`, which exports as `RemoteMaterialTheme.colorScheme.<role>`.

propertyCapabilities.name: fontVariationSettings
propertyCapabilities.notes: Variable-font axis coordinates, CSS `font-variation-settings` style with bare tags: `wght 650, wdth 87.5, GRAD -50`. Written as `RemoteText(fontVariationSettings = FontVariation.Settings(…))`, so the document carries the axes and the player applies them to the face it resolves; an axis that face does not have is ignored. `wght` set here overrides `fontWeight`.

propertyCapabilities.name: fontFeatureSettings
propertyCapabilities.notes: OpenType layout features, CSS `font-feature-settings` style with bare tags: `tnum, ss01, liga 0`. Written as `style = ….merge(fontFeatureSettings = …)`, since `RemoteText` has no feature parameter; Remote Compose carries them in the document beside the axes. A feature the typeface does not have is ignored.

propertyCapabilities.name: pageCount
propertyCapabilities.notes: How many pages there are; 4 when absent. `state` is a `RemotePageIndicatorState`, which no design value becomes, so the emitter builds it from this and `selectedPage`.

propertyCapabilities.name: selectedPage
propertyCapabilities.notes: The page shown, from zero: a literal or the design's Int state, which is how a pager drives the dots. The first when absent.

frame.$comment_adapter: Not a screen. A Remote Compose widget is drawn into a host container of a fixed size, so the frame is the host, not a watch face: `frame/widget-host` rather than the sibling catalog's `frame/round-screen`. This is the second reason `remote-m3` is a catalog of its own rather than a mode of the Wear one.

geometry.$comment: The two host sizes are DECLARED BY THE PREVIEW CONTRACT, not measured after the fact: remote-catalog/src/main/kotlin/ee/schimke/wearm3catalog/remote/WidgetContainerPreviews.kt pins @Preview(widthDp = 216, heightDp = 76) and (216, 124), being 200x60dp and 200x108dp of content plus 8dp of padding on every edge. Every widget sticker in this catalog renders at one of them, so they are the sizes a builder must offer. Recorded here rather than transcribed into the server, which carried both numbers as constants.

native.reason: The generated creation-DSL Kotlin compiled against this module's own alpha Remote Compose trio and rasterised by the real player — the same lane that produces every sticker in this catalog.

wasm.reason: The selectable Visual Editor draws Wear Compose CMP stand-ins. The read-only Browser Preview is a separate DEVICE surface: CMP Remote M3 records a real .rc document in Wasm and the pinned CMP RcComposePlayer plays it in each selected host frame. Approximate describes authoring only, never the Browser Preview.
